Mutations in TCN2 (transcobalamin II) and LMBRD1 impair the cellular uptake and intracellular processing of cobalamin (Vitamin B12), respectively. This leads to a deficiency in active cobalamin, which is essential as a cofactor for methionine synthase (involved in the methionine cycle and homocysteine remethylation) and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (involved in the methylmalonyl-CoA pathway).
